Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated in a CNN interview that his country faces a severe shortage of Patriot interceptor missiles amidst surging Russian ballistic attacks, relying on opaque deal-making to secure supplies.

The Poison:
The reliance on opaque, backdoor deal-making erodes institutional trust and highlights vulnerabilities in international allied supply chains.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The analysis mistakes the physical capability of interceptor missiles (WHAT) for the diplomatic authority and global supply allocation (WHO). It is a structural bottleneck rather than a simple transaction.

Social Physics Analysis:
Survival imperatives drive leaders toward opaque bilateral deals rather than transparent coalitions, concentrating friction and raising systemic risks.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Δ(p·t + n) < 0 due to resource scarcity.

The Unavoidable Truth: Ukraine faces a catastrophic deficit in air defense interceptors.

The Unavoidable Lie: A simple 10% missile purchase can single-handedly eradicate all ballistic attacks.

Metrics show a stark gap between diplomatic rhetoric and logistical reality. The supply deficit is real, but the framing of a total fix via one transaction oversimplifies global defense constraints.
